speaker: ALEX
text: Systemic risk is the technical term there. It means one failure that triggers a chain of other failures across the whole financial system. The 2008 financial crisis is the most well-known example of what systemic risk looks like when it goes wrong.

speaker: JAMIE
text: And here's what nobody says out loud — the companies most exposed are often the ones with the biggest announcements. The louder the data center buildout, the larger the debt load behind it.

speaker: RUFUS
text: The FSB exists specifically because of 2008. Its entire purpose is to prevent that kind of cascading failure. So when the FSB says agentic AI poses unique systemic risks, that's not routine regulatory caution. That's the body designed to see this problem early, saying it sees it.

speaker: RUFUS
text: Risk-based triggers for human intervention. The idea is that financial firms need to define in advance — not in theory, but in their actual systems — the conditions under which a human has to approve what an AI agent is about to do. Particularly in high-risk automated workflows.
